key_insight: Careful circuit optimization on a superconducting processor can measurably suppress logical errors in a surface-code memory, but the benefit depends strongly on qubit quality and implementation details.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that hardware-aware co-design of readout, reset, and echo sequences can improve near-term quantum error correction performance on cloud-accessible devices.
method: Tested rotated surface-code memory on IBM Nighthawk r2 at multiple processor placements
Optimized syndrome extraction with short readout, fused measurement/reset, and XX echo on data qubits
Compared logical error rates across code distances and memory rounds using maximum-likelihood decoding
evidence_signal: The optimized circuit reduced median per-round logical error by 3.8× in the X basis and 1.4× in the Z basis, and increasing distance from 3 to 6 lowered per-round logical error from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory.
watch_item: The distance advantage weakened over long memory runs, suggesting persistent correlated errors or other non-ideal noise sources may limit scaling.
paper_title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
